_comment: World-AGNOSTIC modern-term dictionary for the anachronism bridge. The Facilitator SPEAKS modern_sense; the Representative is handed only underlying_subject (term-free, world-agnostic) and answers in its own world's terms. Disposition is NOT stored per world - it is derived generically: the bridge fires only when a term's origin_year postdates the seated world's end year (parsed from the manifest 'period'). No per-world authoring. Design: Ministry/Technology/CiC_Anachronism_Bridge_Spec_V0_1.md.

display_terms: he died in our place for our sins
terms.modern_sense: the idea, held especially in Reformed and evangelical Protestant traditions, that on the cross Christ bore in the sinner's place the punishment their sins deserved, satisfying the justice of God, so that those who trust him are counted right with God
terms.period_originated: the Reformation, sixteenth century (the substitution idea is older; this systematized penal form is not)
terms.underlying_subject: what the death of Christ accomplished - what it secured, and how your world spoke of it

display_terms: is Jesus your personal Lord and Savior
terms.modern_sense: the way much of modern evangelical Christianity speaks of faith as an individual, personal relationship with Jesus that one has and grows in
terms.underlying_subject: what it meant to belong to Christ, and the shape of a life given to him

terms.modern_sense: the Reformation principle that a person is put right with God through faith alone, not by anything they do
terms.underlying_subject: how a person came to be, and to stay, right with God - the place of faith and of what one does

display_terms: the Bible is the only authority
terms.modern_sense: the Reformation principle that Scripture alone is the final authority for faith, above church tradition and church office
terms.underlying_subject: where authority rested when something had to be settled - Scripture, tradition, a teacher, or an office

terms.modern_sense: the classical doctrine that the one God is Father, Son, and Holy Spirit - three who are each fully God, yet one God, not three - worked out in the precise technical language of the fourth-century councils
terms.underlying_subject: how the Father, the Son, and the Spirit were spoken of and held together

terms.modern_sense: the developed doctrine that all people inherit from Adam a fallen nature - and, in its harder forms, inherited guilt - so that they are born in sin and need grace to be restored
terms.underlying_subject: the roots and reach of sin in a person - whether it is inherited or chosen, and what it takes to be freed of it

display_terms: the bread becomes the actual body
terms.modern_sense: the teaching that in Communion the bread and wine truly become, in their inner reality, the body and blood of Christ, even while they still look and taste like bread and wine
terms.period_originated: the high Middle Ages (term and metaphysics, Lateran IV 1215)
terms.underlying_subject: what your world understood the bread and the cup of the shared meal to be

terms.modern_sense: in modern revivalist Christianity, an identity marking a person who has undergone a conscious conversion to personal faith in Christ
terms.period_originated: eighteenth-to-twentieth-century revivalism (the phrase itself is ancient)
terms.underlying_subject: what changed for a person when they came to faith, and how that change showed in their life

terms.modern_sense: in dispensationalist theology, the belief that believers will be suddenly caught up to meet Christ before a final period of tribulation on earth
terms.underlying_subject: how the end of things and Christ's return were understood, if your world spoke of them at all

display_terms: a state of purification after death
terms.modern_sense: the doctrine of a state of purification after death for those destined for heaven but not yet fully cleansed
terms.period_originated: defined in the high-to-late Middle Ages (Lyons 1274, Florence, Trent)
terms.underlying_subject: what your world understood to happen to a person after death
